simple.meaning: מִגְדָּנָה (migdânâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “preciousness , i.e. a gem.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 24:53. The surrounding context includes birth, family, firstborn, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִגְדָּנָה (H4030) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מִגְדָּנָה (migdânâh) / H4030 is traced through Genesis 24:53, 2 Chronicles 21:3, 2 Chronicles 32:23, Ezra 1:6 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The servant brought out jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious things to her brother and her mother.

majorEvents.evidenceText: All those who were around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, with animals, and with precious things, in addition to all that was willingly offered.

timeline.evidenceText: The servant brought out jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious things to her brother and her mother.
Their father gave them great gifts of silver, of gold, and of precious things, with fortified cities in Judah; but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
Many brought gifts to Yahweh to Jerusalem, and precious things to Hezekiah king of Judah; so that he was exalted in the sight of all nations from then on.
All those who were around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, with animals, and with precious things, in addition to all that was willingly offered.
